question: Do the two already frozen controls keep the action on original task singular directions small, rather than merely assign most parameter energy to a large complement?
coordinate_convention: Original expert-minus-public-base task matrix. Native PyTorch matrix axes; Q/K/V split; patch convolution flattened as its linear patch map. Fixed rank32. No rotation/reselection of the original basis.
measurement: Right-input span and paired rank-one span reported separately, including their dimensions, complement energy, absolute/relative response change, singular cutoff gap, and all74 matrices. Bias/LN/embeddings excluded and not conflated with full-model D.
independent_checks: NumPy projection norms, orthogonal energy identity and both SVD equations at1e-8; save actual basis once. Afterward a separate NumPy process reopens frozen checkpoints and recomputes every row.
access: Defender-side diagnostic uses original expert, public base and two frozen releases only. No images, partner, test logits, gradients, parameter changes or new attack calls. No candidate/strength/rank selection from this result.
scope: Known controls only; not a new defense algorithm, TSV compression reproduction or task-functional guarantee.
zero_task_policy: Stop if a selected task matrix is exactly zero; do not invent task directions.

references.adaptation: Matrix task-vector definition and SVD only; rank32 is this project probe, not a paper default or new algorithm.
